ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An equilateral triangle is originally painted black. Each time the triangle is changed, the middle fourth of each black triangle turns white. After five changes, what fractional part of the original area of the black triangle remains black?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows, from left to right, the process of change of an equilateral triangle. The leftmost triangle is completely colored black; after Change 1, the small inverted triangle in the middle becomes white, and the remaining same-sized triangles at the three corners are still black; after Change 2, inside each small triangle that is still black, the middle one fourth is again made white in the same way. Reasoning: At each change, each black triangle is divided into 4 equal small triangles, among which the 1 in the middle becomes white, and the remaining 3 are still black. Therefore after each change, the black area is multiplied by 3/4. The original black area accounts for 1 of the original figure, and after five changes the remaining black area proportion is (3/4)^5 = 3^5/4^5 = 243/1024.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram left to right: the initial equilateral triangle is fully black; after Change 1, a central inverted triangle is white and three congruent corner triangles remain black; after Change 2, the same central removal pattern is applied inside each remaining black corner triangle. From the text, note that this operation is repeated for five changes and that the removed part each time is the middle fourth of every black triangle. Use the self-similar area rule: each black triangle keeps 3 of its 4 equal subtriangles, so the total black area is multiplied by 3/4 at every change. Starting from area fraction 1, after five changes the black fraction is (3/4)^5 = 243/1024.
